provenance.event: Apollo 12 lunar module ascent stage (Intrepid) deliberate impact
provenance.eventDescription: After Pete Conrad and Alan Bean returned to the command module Yankee Clipper, the empty ascent stage of the lunar module Intrepid was jettisoned, and controllers commanded it to fire its thrusters to drop out of orbit and crash into the Moon, giving the seismometer a known impact to study. NASA notes the seismometer recorded signals for nearly one hour after the impact.

impact.timeConvention: Earth-received time (NSSDCA: about 1.3 s later than on the Moon), the same convention as the seismic timestamps
impact.distanceNote: Great-circle distance computed by this script from the NSSDCA impact coordinates and the IRIS station coordinates (Moon radius 1737.4 km). NASA pages round it differently (NSSDCA spacecraft page: about 60 km; NASA History: about 40 miles).

provenance.instrument: Apollo 12 Passive Seismic Experiment (PSE), part of ALSEP
provenance.locationMeaning: peaked-mode response (location 00 = peaked mode, 01 = flat mode)
provenance.channelMeaning: mid-period vertical seismometer (called "long-period" in older papers)
provenance.timeConvention: Earth-received UTC: the time the signal reached the ground station; the ~1.2-1.4 s Moon-to-Earth light time is not removed (Nunn et al. 2022).
provenance.sampleRateNote: Nominal rate (sample interval 0.1509434 s). The archive notes the true rate varies slightly.
provenance.units: counts (raw digital units of the 10-bit PSE digitiser; not converted to ground motion)

nominalSensitivity.units: counts per metre of ground displacement at 1 Hz
nominalSensitivity.note: Nominal value from IRIS/EarthScope StationXML ("Sensor responses contain nominal values"); not applied to the samples.

provenance.availabilityNote: The FDSN availability service (https://service.iris.edu/fdsnws/availability/1/query?net=XA&sta=S12&loc=00&cha=MHZ&start=1969-11-20T22%3A12%3A00&end=1969-11-20T23%3A22%3A00) answered HTTP 404 ("This service has been retired"), so gaps were found from the data itself: timestamp jumps between records and the archive's -1 fill value.

citations: Apollo Passive Seismic Experiments, FDSN network XA, doi:10.7914/SN/XA_1969, data from the EarthScope (IRIS) Data Management Center.
Nunn, C. et al. (2022), A New Archive of Apollo's Lunar Seismic Data, Planetary Science Journal 3, 219, doi:10.3847/PSJ/ac87af.
NASA NSSDCA, Lunar Impact Sites (Impact Sites of Apollo LM Ascent and SIVB Stages), impact data from Toksoz et al. 1974.
notes: These are the actual measured samples from the Apollo 12 seismometer, not synthesized sound.
A seismometer measures ground vibration, not sound in air (the Moon has no air). Speeding the vibration up is a chosen transformation that makes it audible.

In this recording the shaking rises above the background about 18 s after the impact time (first 5 s window over 4x the pre-impact RMS), is strongest about 5 minutes after impact, then fades slowly over most of an hour.
0 overlapping duplicate samples were dropped while gridding.
Window ends at 23:22 UTC; an unrelated large slow swing on this channel starts at about 23:27 UTC.

transform.gapHandling: Missing samples left as null (JSON) / 0 = silence (audio); never interpolated across.

detrend.method: least-squares mean and linear trend removed, valid samples only

filter.method: high-pass by subtracting a centred running mean of valid samples
filter.why: Removes slow drift (mainly a ~60 s instrument swing) that is below hearing after speed-up but would otherwise use up the loudness range.

normalization.method: divide by peak absolute value after filtering

transform.quantization: JSON samples rounded to 4 decimals; multiply by countsPerUnit to get filtered counts
transform.audioSampleRateNote: Each measured sample becomes one audio sample at 1325 samples/s (6.625 x 200). Players need a standard rate, so makeAudioBuffer() and the WAV interpolate to the device/file rate with a Lanczos-3 kernel; pitch and timing are unchanged.
